today_in_history_posts.title: Draft BIP for SNICKER
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The proposed solution uses encrypted transactions with shared secrets to handle coinjoin and watch-only issues.  - Classic watch-only wallets are incompatible, but real-time SNICKER transaction monitoring can be achieved securely.  - Security concerns and cryptographic choices, including AES-GCM versus AES-CBC, were discussed and found useful.

today_in_history_posts.title: Data Lightning Atomic Swap (DLAS-down, DLAS-up)
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The Data Lightning Atomic Swap enables atomic data and lightning payment exchanges in two patterns.  - DLAS-down swaps data-download for payment, needing improved scalability; DLAS-up swaps data-upload, requiring OG AMP.  - The mechanism does not address data validity checks but explains atomic exchanges via the Lightning Network.

today_in_history_posts.title: Segwit Ephemeral Anchors
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Ephemeral Anchors allow key-less outputs, but Bitcoin's legacy script exposes them to transaction malleability.  - An initial wsh(OP_TRUE) solution is inefficient and leaks unnecessary information through extra bytes and scripts.  - A segwit-based method uses a modified witness program to reduce overhead and simplify spending rules.
